n: A new section begins: the family record of Adam. It reminds us that humans were made in God’s likeness. The book of Moses mentions that Adam’s family kept a “book of remembrance.”

f.w: the book of the generations of Adam

n: Men and women together are blessed by God and called “Adam,” meaning humankind. Both share the dignity of being created by God.

f.g: Hebrew ’adam can mean “mankind” as well as the first man’s name.

n: Seth is born “in Adam’s image,” echoing how Adam was made in God’s image. The family likeness passes from God to Adam to Seth, linking all generations to God.

f.w: in his own likeness, after his image

n: Adam lives many more years and has many children. Genealogies like this show that God’s blessing to multiply was being fulfilled.

f.g: Only key sons are named, but large families are implied.

n: Adam dies at 930, fulfilling the warning that death would come. Shortly before his death, restoration scripture says, Adam gathered his righteous posterity at Adam-ondi-Ahman and blessed them.
Seth becomes father to Enos. The repeated pattern—age at fatherhood, years after, total years—gives the chapter a steady, rhythmic feel.
Seth continues to live and raise a large family for centuries after Enos’s birth.

f.g: These long lifespans are a striking feature of the pre-Flood generations.

n: Seth dies at 912. The refrain “and he died” echoes through the chapter, reminding readers that mortality now touches every life.

f.g: Repeated eight times in this chapter—with one striking exception (verse 24).

n: Enos fathers Cainan. Doctrine and Covenants 107 adds that these patriarchs received priesthood ordination in their generations.
Enos lives on for centuries, raising a large family.

f.g: Became the father of; sometimes means ancestor of.

n: Enos dies at 905.

f.g: Total years of Enos’s life.

n: Cainan fathers Mahalaleel, whose name praises God—hinting at the faith of this family line.

f.g: Means “praise of God.”

n: Cainan lives on and has many children.

f.g: Years Cainan lived after Mahalaleel’s birth.

n: Cainan dies at 910.

f.g: Cainan’s total lifespan.

n: Mahalaleel fathers Jared.

f.g: Means “descent” or “coming down.”

n: Mahalaleel lives on and raises sons and daughters.

f.g: Years Mahalaleel lived after Jared’s birth.

n: Mahalaleel dies at 895.

f.w: eight hundred ninety and five years
f.g: Mahalaleel’s total lifespan.

n: Jared fathers Enoch, one of the greatest prophets of the early world. The book of Moses records Enoch’s ministry in rich detail.
Jared lives on and raises a large family. The book of Moses says Jared taught Enoch “in all the ways of God.”
Jared lives 962 years, the second-longest lifespan recorded.

f.w: nine hundred sixty and two years
f.g: Only Methuselah lived longer (verse 27).

n: Enoch fathers Methuselah at sixty-five.

f.g: The name may mean “man of the spear” or “man sent forth.”

n: Enoch “walked with God”—a lovely phrase for living in close, daily fellowship with the Lord. He did so while raising a family.

f.g: Lived in close companionship and obedience with God.

n: Enoch’s 365 years is much shorter than his relatives’ lifespans, but his life does not end in ordinary death.

f.w: three hundred sixty and five years

n: Instead of “and he died,” Enoch simply “was not; for God took him.” Restoration scripture teaches that Enoch and his city of Zion were taken into heaven because of their righteousness.
Methuselah fathers Lamech.

f.g: A different man from the violent Lamech of Cain’s line (4:18-24).

n: Methuselah lives on for centuries and raises a large family. The book of Moses says he was not taken with Enoch so that God’s covenant through his line could be fulfilled.
Methuselah lives 969 years, the longest life in the Bible. By the chapter’s numbers, he died in the year of the Flood.

f.w: nine hundred sixty and nine years
f.g: The oldest age recorded in scripture.

n: Lamech fathers a son at 182.

f.g: The son is named in the next verse.

n: Lamech names his son Noah, hoping he will bring relief from the hard toil caused by the curse on the ground. Noah will indeed bring rest and a new beginning.

f.g: Sounds like Hebrew nuaḥ, “rest,” and is linked here to naḥam, “comfort.”

f.w: the ground which the LORD hath cursed

n: Lamech lives on and raises other children.

f.w: five hundred ninety and five years
f.g: Years Lamech lived after Noah’s birth.

n: Lamech dies at 777—a number some see as fitting, in contrast to the boastful “seventy and sevenfold” of Cain’s Lamech.

f.w: seven hundred seventy and seven years

n: Noah becomes father to Shem, Ham, and Japheth, the three sons through whom the earth will be repopulated after the Flood. The stage is set for the next great chapter.
